about: Topic map of the AP Psychology Course and Exam Description (effective fall 2025, with the October 2025 clarifications; the 2024-25 framework, not revised for 2026-27), written in LevlPrep's own words from docs/appsych-research/framework.md. Every topic title is official (Course at a Glance). Objectives and knowledge are our summaries; for 2.7 to 5.5 they come from a third-party copy of the CED codes and are marked in source. No CED text is reproduced.

ced.title: AP Psychology Course and Exam Description
ced.edition: Effective Fall 2025 (5 units, 35 topics), with the clarifications and corrections implemented October 2025
ced.verification: All 35 titles from the Course at a Glance (agrees with every title the CED extract showed, 1.1 to 2.6). CED text readable into Topic 2.6; objectives for 2.7 to 5.5 third party (Lumisource copies of the CED codes). Practice weights in Section I third party (Fiveable, Achievable). Read 2026-10-27.

skillNames.1.A: Apply psychological perspectives, theories, concepts and research findings to a scenario
skillNames.1.B: Explain how cultural norms, expectations and cognitive biases apply to behavior and mental processes

skillNames.2.A: Identify the research method and design of a study, and what it can conclude
skillNames.2.B: Evaluate the elements of an experimental design: hypothesis, operational definitions, variables, groups
skillNames.2.C: Evaluate the elements of a non-experimental design: correlation direction, third variables, survey wording, self-report
skillNames.2.D: Identify the ethical safeguards a study used and how the researchers applied them

skillNames.3.A: Identify psychological concepts in a table, graph or figure
skillNames.3.B: Calculate and interpret central tendency, variation and percentile rank
skillNames.3.C: Interpret inferential statistics: statistical significance and effect size

skillNames.4.B: Provide reasoning grounded in evidence to support, refute or modify a claim

topics.title: Interaction of Heredity and Environment
objectives: Explain how heredity and environment interact to shape behavior and mental processes, and how twin, family and adoption studies separate them.
knowledge: Behavior comes from genes and experience working together, never one alone.
The evolutionary perspective explains traits by the survival and reproduction advantages they gave; misusing it to rank people led to eugenics.
Twin, family and adoption studies compare how alike relatives are to estimate how much of a trait's variation is linked to genes.
exclusions: Genetics vocabulary (genotype, phenotype, DNA, chromosomes, dominant and recessive alleles) is out of scope.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge summarized from the CED unit pages (docs/appsych-research/framework.md section 3)

topics.title: Overview of the Nervous System
objectives: Describe how the central and peripheral nervous systems, and the somatic and autonomic divisions, organize behavior.
knowledge: The central nervous system is the brain and spinal cord; the peripheral nervous system connects it to the body.
The somatic system moves skeletal muscles; the autonomic system runs the body automatically, with a sympathetic arousing division and a parasympathetic calming division.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge summarized from the CED unit pages (docs/appsych-research/framework.md section 3)

topics.title: The Neuron and Neural Firing
objectives: Explain how a neuron fires and how neurotransmitters, hormones and psychoactive drugs change communication between neurons.
knowledge: A neuron fires when depolarization passes threshold: the action potential is all-or-none and is followed by a refractory period; neurotransmitters cross the synapse and are taken back by reuptake.

Named neurotransmitters (dopamine, serotonin, norepinephrine, glutamate, GABA, endorphins, substance P, acetylcholine) and hormones (adrenaline, leptin, ghrelin, melatonin, oxytocin) each have characteristic effects.

Agonists mimic or strengthen a neurotransmitter, antagonists block it, reuptake inhibitors keep it in the synapse longer; repeated use brings tolerance and withdrawal. Multiple sclerosis and myasthenia gravis show what happens when signaling fails.
exclusions: The sodium-potassium pump is out of scope; only the listed neurotransmitters, hormones and the pituitary among endocrine glands.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge summarized from the CED unit pages (docs/appsych-research/framework.md section 3)

topics.title: The Brain
objectives: Explain how brain structures relate to behavior and mental processes, and how researchers study the brain.
knowledge: The brainstem and medulla keep the body alive; the reticular activating system controls arousal and alertness; the cerebellum coordinates movement; the reward center drives motivation.

The cortex has four lobes with specialized areas (motor, somatosensory, Broca's and Wernicke's areas); limbic structures (thalamus, hypothalamus, pituitary, hippocampus, amygdala) handle relay, drives, memory and emotion.

Each hemisphere controls the opposite side of the body; split-brain cases show what the corpus callosum does; the brain rewires through plasticity. EEG, fMRI, case studies and lesioning reveal function.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge summarized from a third-party copy of the CED codes [3P], to verify against the CED (docs/appsych-needs-author.md, ced-text)

topics.title: Sleep
objectives: Explain the stages and functions of sleep, theories of dreaming and common sleep disorders.
knowledge: Consciousness varies across a circadian rhythm; sleep cycles through NREM stages and REM about every 90 minutes.
Sleep restores the body and consolidates memories; dreaming is explained by activation-synthesis and consolidation theories.
Listed disorders: insomnia, narcolepsy, REM sleep behavior disorder, sleep apnea, somnambulism.
exclusions: Psychoanalytic dream theory; sleep disorders beyond the listed five.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge summarized from the CED unit pages (docs/appsych-research/framework.md section 3)

topics.title: Sensation
objectives: Explain how the senses detect and transduce energy, and the theories that explain vision, hearing, the chemical senses, touch, pain and body position.
knowledge: Thresholds (absolute, just-noticeable difference, Weber's law), signal detection, sensory adaptation and interaction govern what is noticed.
Vision uses rods and cones and is explained by trichromatic and opponent-process theories; hearing by place, frequency and volley theories; deafness is conduction or sensorineural.
Smell and taste (including umami and oleogustus), touch, pain (gate control, phantom limbs), and the vestibular and kinesthetic senses complete the senses.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge summarized from a third-party copy of the CED codes [3P], to verify against the CED (docs/appsych-needs-author.md, ced-text)

topics.title: Perception
objectives: Explain how internal and external factors shape perception, and how the visual system builds depth, form and motion.
knowledge: Bottom-up and top-down processing, schemas and perceptual set shape what is perceived; selective attention filters input (cocktail party effect, change blindness).
Gestalt principles (closure, figure-ground, proximity, similarity) organize form; binocular and monocular cues give depth; constancies keep objects stable; apparent movement creates motion.
exclusions: Only the monocular cues the CED lists.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge summarized from the CED unit pages (docs/appsych-research/framework.md section 3)

topics.title: Thinking, Problem-Solving, Judgments, and Decision-Making
objectives: Explain how concepts, problem-solving strategies and cognitive biases affect thinking and decisions.
knowledge: Concepts and prototypes organize knowledge; schemas grow by assimilation and accommodation.

Algorithms guarantee a solution; heuristics (representativeness, availability) are fast but biased; mental set, functional fixedness, priming, framing, the gambler's fallacy and the sunk-cost fallacy distort judgment.
Executive functions and creativity, including divergent thinking, support problem-solving.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge summarized from the CED unit pages (docs/appsych-research/framework.md section 3)

topics.title: Introduction to Memory
objectives: Describe the kinds of memory and the models that explain how memory works.
knowledge: Explicit memory (episodic, semantic) and implicit memory (procedural) differ; prospective memory remembers to act.
The multi-store model and the working memory model describe stages and components; long-term potentiation strengthens synapses; processing is automatic or effortful, shallow or deep.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge summarized from the CED unit pages (docs/appsych-research/framework.md section 3)

topics.title: Encoding Memories
objectives: Explain strategies that improve encoding.
knowledge: Mnemonics, the method of loci, chunking and hierarchies organize information.
Distributed practice beats massed practice (the spacing effect); the serial position effect favors the first and last items.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge summarized from the CED unit pages (docs/appsych-research/framework.md section 3)

topics.title: Storing Memories
objectives: Explain how memories are stored and what disrupts storage.
knowledge: Maintenance rehearsal keeps information briefly; elaborative rehearsal links it to meaning for long-term storage.
Retrograde and anterograde amnesia, Alzheimer's disease and infantile amnesia show storage failing; superior autobiographical memory shows its other extreme.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge summarized from the CED unit pages (docs/appsych-research/framework.md section 3)

topics.title: Retrieving Memories
objectives: Explain how retrieval works and how to strengthen it.
knowledge: Recall and recognition differ; context-, state- and mood-dependent memory show cues matter.
Retrieval practice and the testing effect strengthen memory; metacognition is judging what you know.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge summarized from the CED unit pages (docs/appsych-research/framework.md section 3)

topics.title: Forgetting and Other Memory Challenges
objectives: Explain why people forget and how memories are distorted.
knowledge: The forgetting curve, encoding failure, proactive and retroactive interference and the tip-of-the-tongue state explain forgetting; repression is the psychodynamic account.
Memory is constructive: the misinformation effect, source amnesia and imagination inflation create false memories.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge summarized from a third-party copy of the CED codes [3P], to verify against the CED (docs/appsych-needs-author.md, ced-text)

topics.title: Intelligence and Achievement
objectives: Explain theories and measurement of intelligence, the systemic issues in testing, and achievement.
knowledge: General intelligence contrasts with multiple abilities; the IQ score, standardization, reliability and validity describe a good test.
Stereotype threat and lift, the Flynn effect, within- and between-group variation and the historical misuse of tests show systemic issues.
Achievement and aptitude tests differ; fixed and growth mindsets affect effort.
exclusions: Labeling or describing cognitive abilities and disabilities.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge summarized from a third-party copy of the CED codes [3P], to verify against the CED (docs/appsych-needs-author.md, ced-text)

topics.title: Themes and Methods in Developmental Psychology
objectives: Explain the major themes and research designs of developmental psychology.
knowledge: Stability and change, nature and nurture, continuity and discontinuity frame development.
Cross-sectional studies compare age groups at one time; longitudinal studies follow one group over time.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge summarized from a third-party copy of the CED codes [3P], to verify against the CED (docs/appsych-needs-author.md, ced-text)

topics.title: Physical Development Across the Lifespan
objectives: Explain physical development from before birth through adulthood.
knowledge: Teratogens harm prenatal development; reflexes and motor milestones mark infancy; critical and sensitive periods and imprinting show timing matters; the visual cliff tests depth perception.
Puberty brings primary and secondary sex characteristics, menarche and spermarche; adulthood brings sensory and motor change and menopause.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge summarized from a third-party copy of the CED codes [3P], to verify against the CED (docs/appsych-needs-author.md, ced-text)

topics.title: Gender and Sexual Orientation
objectives: Explain how sex and gender influence socialization and development.
knowledge: Biological sex and gender differ; gender roles and gender typing come from socialization; sexual orientation is a distinct dimension.
exclusions: Learning objectives not read directly (docs/appsych-needs-author.md, ced-text).
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge summarized from a third-party copy of the CED codes [3P], to verify against the CED (docs/appsych-needs-author.md, ced-text)

topics.title: Cognitive Development Across the Lifespan
objectives: Explain how thinking develops from infancy through old age.
knowledge: Piaget's stages (sensorimotor, preoperational, concrete and formal operational) are marked by object permanence, conservation, egocentrism and theory of mind.
Vygotsky's zone of proximal development and scaffolding stress social support; in adulthood crystallized intelligence holds while fluid intelligence declines; dementia is disease, not normal aging.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge summarized from a third-party copy of the CED codes [3P], to verify against the CED (docs/appsych-needs-author.md, ced-text)

topics.title: Communication and Language Development
objectives: Describe the parts of language and how children acquire it.
knowledge: Language has phonemes, morphemes, semantics, grammar and syntax, and is generative.
Children move from cooing and babbling to one-word and telegraphic speech, and overgeneralize rules.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge summarized from a third-party copy of the CED codes [3P], to verify against the CED (docs/appsych-needs-author.md, ced-text)

topics.title: Social-Emotional Development Across the Lifespan
objectives: Explain social and emotional development across the lifespan.
knowledge: Ecological systems theory nests influences; parenting styles and attachment styles (secure, avoidant, anxious, disorganized) shape relationships; contact comfort mattered more than food in monkey studies.
The eight psychosocial stages, identity statuses, the imaginary audience and personal fable, emerging adulthood and the social clock mark later development; adverse childhood experiences raise risk.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge summarized from a third-party copy of the CED codes [3P], to verify against the CED (docs/appsych-needs-author.md, ced-text)

topics.title: Classical Conditioning
objectives: Explain how classical conditioning creates learned associations.
knowledge: A neutral stimulus paired with an unconditioned stimulus becomes a conditioned stimulus that triggers a conditioned response; acquisition, extinction, spontaneous recovery, generalization and discrimination follow.
Higher-order conditioning, counterconditioning, one-trial taste aversion and biological preparedness extend it; habituation is the simplest learning.
exclusions: Delayed, trace, simultaneous and backward conditioning; expectancy theory.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge summarized from a third-party copy of the CED codes [3P], to verify against the CED (docs/appsych-needs-author.md, ced-text)

topics.title: Operant Conditioning
objectives: Explain how consequences shape behavior.
knowledge: The law of effect; positive and negative reinforcement increase behavior, positive and negative punishment decrease it; reinforcers are primary or secondary.

Shaping, instinctive drift, superstitious behavior and learned helplessness; continuous and partial schedules (fixed-ratio, variable-ratio, fixed-interval, variable-interval) produce characteristic response curves.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge summarized from a third-party copy of the CED codes [3P], to verify against the CED (docs/appsych-needs-author.md, ced-text)

topics.title: Social, Cognitive, and Neurological Factors in Learning
objectives: Explain learning through observation and cognition.
knowledge: Social learning works through modeling and vicarious conditioning.
Insight learning, latent learning and cognitive maps show learning without reinforcement at the time.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge summarized from a third-party copy of the CED codes [3P], to verify against the CED (docs/appsych-needs-author.md, ced-text)

topics.title: Attribution Theory and Person Perception
objectives: Explain how people explain behavior and perceive others and themselves.
knowledge: Dispositional and situational attributions; the fundamental attribution error, actor-observer bias and self-serving bias; explanatory style; internal and external locus of control.
The mere exposure effect, self-fulfilling prophecy, upward and downward social comparison and relative deprivation shape person perception.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge summarized from a third-party copy of the CED codes [3P], to verify against the CED (docs/appsych-needs-author.md, ced-text)

topics.title: Attitude Formation and Attitude Change
objectives: Explain how attitudes form, how prejudice arises and how attitudes change.
knowledge: Stereotypes, cognitive load and implicit attitudes feed prejudice; the just-world phenomenon, out-group homogeneity, in-group bias and ethnocentrism sustain it.
Belief perseverance and confirmation bias resist change; cognitive dissonance can drive it.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge summarized from a third-party copy of the CED codes [3P], to verify against the CED (docs/appsych-needs-author.md, ced-text)

topics.title: Psychology of Social Situations
objectives: Explain how situations and groups influence behavior and helping.
knowledge: Norms and roles; normative and informational influence; persuasion by the central and peripheral routes; the halo effect, foot-in-the-door and door-in-the-face; conformity and obedience; individualism and collectivism.

Group polarization, groupthink, diffusion of responsibility, social loafing, deindividuation and social facilitation; false consensus, superordinate goals and social traps; industrial-organizational psychology and burnout.
Altruism, the reciprocity and social responsibility norms, and the bystander effect explain helping.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge summarized from a third-party copy of the CED codes [3P], to verify against the CED (docs/appsych-needs-author.md, ced-text)

topics.title: Psychodynamic and Humanistic Theories of Personality
objectives: Explain psychodynamic and humanistic views of personality and how they are assessed.
knowledge: The psychodynamic view stresses the unconscious and eight defense mechanisms, assessed with projective tests.
The humanistic view stresses unconditional positive regard and a self-actualizing tendency.
exclusions: Psychosexual stage theory; Maslow's hierarchy of needs (third party, to confirm: docs/appsych-needs-author.md, exclusions).
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge summarized from a third-party copy of the CED codes [3P], to verify against the CED (docs/appsych-needs-author.md, ced-text)

topics.title: Social-Cognitive and Trait Theories of Personality
objectives: Explain social-cognitive and trait views of personality and how traits are measured.
knowledge: Reciprocal determinism links person, behavior and environment; self-concept, self-efficacy and self-esteem.
Trait theories, the Big Five, factor analysis and personality inventories describe and measure personality.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge summarized from a third-party copy of the CED codes [3P], to verify against the CED (docs/appsych-needs-author.md, ced-text)

topics.title: Motivation
objectives: Explain theories of motivation and the motives of eating and belonging.
knowledge: Drive-reduction, arousal (Yerkes-Dodson), self-determination and incentive theories; instincts in non-human animals; motivational conflicts; sensation seeking.
Ghrelin, leptin and external cues affect eating; the need to belong shapes social behavior.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge summarized from a third-party copy of the CED codes [3P], to verify against the CED (docs/appsych-needs-author.md, ced-text)

topics.title: Emotion
objectives: Explain how emotion is experienced, explained and expressed.
knowledge: Theories differ in whether arousal, appraisal and feeling come in sequence or together; the facial feedback hypothesis has mixed evidence; broaden-and-build.
Some emotions are widely recognized across cultures (with mixed evidence); display rules govern expression.
exclusions: Specific names of emotion theories (third party, to confirm: docs/appsych-needs-author.md, exclusions).
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge summarized from a third-party copy of the CED codes [3P], to verify against the CED (docs/appsych-needs-author.md, ced-text)

topics.title: Introduction to Health Psychology
objectives: Explain how stress affects health and how people cope.
knowledge: Stress, eustress and distress; daily hassles and adverse childhood experiences; the general adaptation syndrome; fight-flight-freeze and tend-and-befriend.
Problem-focused and emotion-focused coping.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge summarized from a third-party copy of the CED codes [3P], to verify against the CED (docs/appsych-needs-author.md, ced-text)

topics.title: Positive Psychology
objectives: Explain the factors that support well-being.
knowledge: Positive psychology studies well-being, resilience, gratitude, signature strengths and the six virtue categories; posttraumatic growth.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge summarized from a third-party copy of the CED codes [3P], to verify against the CED (docs/appsych-needs-author.md, ced-text)

topics.title: Explaining and Classifying Psychological Disorders
objectives: Explain how psychological disorders are defined, classified and explained.
knowledge: Disorders involve dysfunction, distress and deviation; the DSM (American Psychiatric Association, now DSM-5-TR) and the ICD (World Health Organization) classify them.
Perspectives explain disorders; the biopsychosocial and diathesis-stress models combine them; the eclectic approach draws on several.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge summarized from a third-party copy of the CED codes [3P], to verify against the CED (docs/appsych-needs-author.md, ced-text)

topics.title: Selection of Categories of Psychological Disorders
objectives: Describe the symptoms and possible causes of representative disorders in each category.
knowledge: Neurodevelopmental (ADHD, autism spectrum disorder); schizophrenia spectrum; depressive (major depressive, persistent depressive); bipolar I and II.

Anxiety (specific phobia, agoraphobia, panic, social anxiety, generalized anxiety, culture-bound examples); obsessive-compulsive and hoarding; dissociative amnesia and dissociative identity disorder; PTSD; anorexia and bulimia nervosa.
Personality disorders in clusters A, B and C.
exclusions: Only the listed disorders, as representative of an introductory treatment.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge summarized from a third-party copy of the CED codes [3P], to verify against the CED (docs/appsych-needs-author.md, ced-text)

topics.title: Treatment of Psychological Disorders
objectives: Explain how disorders are treated, how treatments are judged and the ethics of treatment.
knowledge: Evidence-based practice, the therapeutic alliance, cultural humility, deinstitutionalization and ethical principles.
Psychodynamic, cognitive, behavioral, cognitive-behavioral and humanistic therapies; group and individual formats; what hypnosis can and cannot do.
Medications (antidepressants, anti-anxiety drugs, lithium, antipsychotics and tardive dyskinesia) and other biological treatments (psychosurgery, lesioning, TMS, ECT, the history of lobotomy).
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge summarized from a third-party copy of the CED codes [3P], to verify against the CED (docs/appsych-needs-author.md, ced-text)

skillsTopics.title: Research Methods and Variables
objectives: Identify a study's research method and its variables, and explain what each method can and cannot conclude.
knowledge: Only an experiment, with random assignment to conditions, supports a cause-and-effect conclusion; correlational studies, case studies, naturalistic observation and surveys describe and predict.

Operational definitions say exactly how a variable is measured; confounding variables, placebo effects and experimenter bias are controlled by design (control groups, single- and double-blind procedures).
Science is cumulative and self-correcting: findings are peer reviewed, replicated and combined in meta-analyses; some classic findings have not replicated.

skillsTopics.title: Sampling and Generalizability
objectives: Explain how a sample is drawn and when results generalize to a population.
knowledge: Random sampling gives a representative sample; a biased or convenience sample limits who the results describe.
Random sampling (who is studied) is not random assignment (which condition each person gets).

skillsTopics.title: Correlation and Scatterplots
objectives: Read the direction and strength of a correlation from a coefficient or a scatterplot, and explain why correlation does not show causation.
knowledge: The correlation coefficient r runs from -1 to +1: its sign is the direction, its size the strength.
A third variable or reverse causation can explain a correlation; illusory correlations are relationships perceived where none exist.

skillsTopics.title: Ethics in Research
objectives: Identify the ethical safeguards a study used and explain how the researchers applied them.
knowledge: Institutional review boards approve studies; informed consent (assent for minors), the right to withdraw, confidentiality, protection from harm and debriefing after any deception protect human participants.
Animal research follows its own guidelines for humane care and justified use.

skillsTopics.title: Descriptive Statistics
objectives: Calculate and interpret measures of central tendency and variation from a small data set, by hand.
knowledge: The mean, median and mode describe the center; an outlier pulls the mean toward it, so a skewed distribution is better described by the median.
The range and the standard deviation describe spread; a histogram shows the shape of a frequency distribution.

skillsTopics.title: The Normal Curve and Percentiles
objectives: Locate a score on the normal curve with a z score and the 68-95-99.7 rule, and interpret a percentile rank.
knowledge: In a normal distribution about 68% of scores lie within one standard deviation of the mean, 95% within two and 99.7% within three.
A z score is the number of standard deviations from the mean; a percentile rank is the percent of scores below a given score.

skillsTopics.title: Statistical Significance and Effect Size
objectives: Interpret a statement of statistical significance and of effect size in a study's results.
knowledge: A statistically significant difference is unlikely to be due to chance alone; it does not say the difference is large or important.
Effect size says how big a difference or relationship is; inferential statistics let researchers generalize from a sample to a population.

exam.delivery: Fully digital in Bluebook; free responses typed.

sets: Sets sharing one study description or data display (third party; official counts not published: docs/appsych-needs-author.md, mcq-sets)

types.aaq: Q1 Article Analysis Question, about 25 min: A method, B operational definition, C statistic, D ethical guideline applied, E generalizability, F argumentation (2)
types.ebq: Q2 Evidence-Based Question, about 45 min: A claim, B(i) evidence, B(ii) reasoning (2), C(i) evidence from a different source, C(ii) reasoning with a different concept (2)

exam.calculator: None. Psychology is not in the College Board calculator table.
